slides.texte_overlay:
How to stop feeling awkward
in silence (and finally relax)
Remember silence feels longer to you than to them. Three seconds feel like a minute in your head. For everyone else, it's just a normal pause. Nobody is counting but you.
Give yourself something to do. Take a sip, look around the room, check out the menu. A small action makes a pause feel natural instead of like everyone's waiting for you.
Comment on something real. "This place has great music." A simple observation restarts a conversation without forcing a deep question nobody wants to answer.
I used to panic in every silence. Now I do five minutes a day of history, art or science, and when a pause comes, I've always got a little story or fun fact ready.
slides.texte_sophia: I used to panic in every silence. Then I started five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. Now I've always got a little story ready.

slides.texte_overlay: Enjoy the quiet with people you know. Good friends can sit together without talking. If silence feels fine with someone, it usually means you're actually comfortable together.
Smile during the pause. A relaxed smile turns an awkward silence into a calm one. It tells the other person you're fine and enjoying yourself, so they relax too and the talk restarts.
Stop judging every gap as failure. Conversations breathe. They go up, slow down, and pick back up. Let them. The less you fear silence, the less awkward it ever feels.
